Context: None

Question: A patient suffers a broken neck with damage to the spinal cord at the level of the sixth cervical vertebra.

Options: 
A. It is impossible to predict an effect on breathing.
B. Their breathing rate will significantly increase.
C. They will only be able to breathe quietly.
D. Their breathing will be erratic and unpredictable.
E. They will be unable to breathe without life support.
F. Breathing will be unaffected.
G. They will be able to breathe only with the help of a ventilator.
H. They will be able to breathe only in short, shallow breaths.
I. They will have to breathe through a tracheostomy tube.
J. They will not be able to breathe out, only in.

Provide the correct letter choice in \boxed{X}, where X is the correct letter choice. Keep the explanation or feedback within 3 sentences.

The spinal cord injury is at the level of the sixth cervical vertebra (C6). The phrenic nerve, which innervates the diaphragm (the primary muscle for inspiration), originates from spinal cord segments C3, C4, and C5. Since the injury is at C6, the phrenic nerve and diaphragm remain functional, allowing the patient to breathe spontaneously. However, the intercostal muscles, which are innervated by thoracic spinal nerves (T1-T11) and are necessary for deep or forced breathing, are paralyzed. Consequently, the patient retains the ability for diaphragmatic (quiet) breathing but loses the ability to perform deep or forced breathing.
